Trader Joe’s Spicy Spuds Review

September 28, 2026September 28, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 7:20
Instaread

Disclosure: This post contains affiliate links. If you buy through them I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. I buy every Trader Joe’s product I review with my own money.

Every bag of frozen potatoes makes the same promise. Crispy outside, fluffy inside, restaurant quality in fifteen minutes. And almost every bag breaks it. You end up with pale, limp, kind of sweaty cubes that taste like the inside of your freezer.

So when Trader Joe’s drops a new frozen potato, I get my hopes up in a very guarded, I’ve been burned before kind of way. I love a new potato because it means more options for dinner sides. But the Spicy Spuds surprised me, because I think they might be even better at breakfast.

Quick dietary note up front, since a lot of you ask. These are not vegan, because there’s parmesan in the seasoning. They’re not gluten free either, because the label lists wheat along with milk. And Trader Joe’s doesn’t list them as kosher. So if you’re shopping for a vegan, celiac or kosher household, I’m sorry, keep scrolling past these in the freezer case. Everyone else, stick around.

What’s in the bag

They’re half inch potato cubes coated in a blend of cayenne pepper, parmesan cheese, lime juice and smoked paprika. On paper that’s four things that have no business working together. In practice they absolutely do.

They look unassuming in the bag, just little frozen cubes with some orange dust on them. Don’t be fooled by the humble appearance. There’s more going on here than you’d think.

These seem to be a regular item, not seasonal. Trader Joe’s didn’t give them the seasonal marker on its website, so hopefully they’re sticking around.

Air fryer is the only way (okay, not the only way)

I threw them in the air fryer because that’s what the air fryer gods intended. Ten minutes at 400 degrees, and I shook the basket a couple of times along the way. That’s it. They came out perfect. Crispy on the outside, fluffy and moist inside, and the seasoning bakes into a spicy, cheesy, slightly tangy shell on every single cube.

Ten minutes, people. That’s less time than it takes to find matching socks for a kid who’s already late for school.

If you don’t own an air fryer, the oven works. You can also sauté them in a pan, and apparently some brave souls deep fry them. But the air fryer is where these really shine, and if you’ve been on the fence about getting one, a bag of these is a pretty good argument. I use a Cosori and it’s handled everything I’ve thrown at it: Cosori Air Fryer at Amazon

One tip. Don’t crowd the basket. Spread them out in a single layer, even if that means cooking in two batches. Piled up potatoes steam instead of crisp, and then you’re right back to sad freezer cubes. Shaking the basket a couple of times helps too, so every side gets its turn at crispy.

The taste (and the lime)

The lime juice is the secret weapon here. You can’t really taste “lime” exactly, but there’s a brightness to the spice blend that keeps it from being one note heat. The smoked paprika adds depth, the cayenne adds a kick, and the parmesan gives it that salty, savory thing that makes you want another bite.

And another. And another. These are the kind of potatoes you eat five more of than you planned, standing over the air fryer telling yourself you’re just “checking if they’re done.” I have checked if they’re done many, many times.

The Taco Bell question

The internet has decided these are a dupe for Taco Bell’s seasoned potatoes, and people are already saying so on social media.

My honest take? I like Taco Bell’s version slightly better. There, I said it. But here’s the thing. I’m lazy, and I am not getting in my car and driving to Taco Bell specifically for a side of spicy potatoes. These are sitting in my freezer, they’re ready in ten minutes, they’re good enough for me, and they’re way cheaper. Close enough wins, especially at 7 AM in your bathrobe.

How to eat them

Honestly, what can’t you do with these?

A plate of eggs, some bacon and a pile of these crispy cubes is a Saturday morning worth waking up for. They’re great next to a burger. Tuck them into tacos or breakfast burritos. Throw them in a cheesy breakfast casserole. People online are building taco bowls on top of them, or swapping them in for rice in breakfast bowls, which is a pretty smart move for anybody trying to mix up meal prep.

Or just put them in a bowl by themselves at 11 PM when you’re watching TV and want something hot and crispy. No judgment here. I’ve been that person.

Portion reality check

A 20 ounce bag sounds like plenty until you realize how snackable these are. As a side for a family dinner, one bag is gone in a single night, especially if teenagers are involved. If you’re feeding a crowd or you know you’re going to “check if they’re done” a few times, grab two bags.

How they stack up against TJ’s other potatoes

Trader Joe’s has a whole frozen potato lineup, including Shredded Potato Hash Browns, Trader Potato Tots, Handsome Cut Potato Fries, Herbes de Provence Potato Wedges, Seasoned Waffle Cut Fries and Sweet Potato Fries. Most of those are a blank canvas that you season yourself or dunk in ketchup. The Spicy Spuds are the only ones I’d happily eat plain, straight out of the basket, because the flavor is already baked in.

Is it worth the money?

At $4.49 for 20 ounces, yes. You’re getting a side dish that’s already seasoned and needs zero effort beyond shaking a basket. For busy weeknights, lazy weekend breakfasts and meal prep, that’s worth a lot more than four and a half bucks. It’s also a lot cheaper than a drive through run.

Quick answers

Are Trader Joe’s Spicy Spuds vegan? No, the seasoning has parmesan cheese.

Are they gluten free? No, the label lists wheat.

Are they kosher? Trader Joe’s doesn’t list them as kosher.

Are they as good as Taco Bell’s potatoes? Close. I like Taco Bell’s slightly better, but these are cheaper and already in my freezer.

How do you cook them in the air fryer? Ten minutes at 400 degrees, shaking the basket a couple of times.

How spicy are they? They have a kick, but it’s balanced by the lime and cheese. Heat seekers might want hot sauce on the side.

Are they seasonal? They don’t seem to be, so they should be around year round.

The verdict

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 9/10

Price: $4.49 for 20 oz

Dietary: Not vegan, not gluten free, not listed as kosher

Best For: Air fryer owners (this is your moment), breakfast lovers, busy parents who need a side dish that overperforms

Skip If: You’re vegan, gluten free or keep kosher, or you want something truly face melting hot

These joined the regular rotation at our house immediately, and I don’t see them leaving anytime soon.
